newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-AMIEZ LEADS, TOMBA REPORTED SICK.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-AMIEZ LEADS, TOMBA REPORTED SICK.

text.p: France's Sebastien Amiez led after the first leg of the men's slalom on Saturday as a feverish Alberto Tomba fought to stay in the medal hunt at the Alpine skiing world championships.
Amiez, who has not won a slalom this season but has finished second once and third three times, twisted his way down the floodlit 67-gate Kandahar course in 54.71 seconds.
Defending champion Tomba lagged 1.50 seconds off the pace and hurried back to his nearby luxury hotel, saying he did not feel well and was exhausted.
Italian reporters said he was being attended by a team doctor and had a temperature. However, he was expected to try to compete in the second leg which starts at 2000 GMT.
Amiez, the reigning World Cup slalom champion, has a commanding 1.02 second advantage over his nearest challenger, Austria's Thomas Sykora, going into the second leg.
Sykora, who has dominated the event this season winning five of eight races, clocked 55.73 while Norway's Tom Stiansen was third-quickest in 55.81.
Austrians occupied three of the top five positions. Olympic champion Thomas Stangassinger was fourth-fastest in 55.92 followed closely by compatriot Mario Reiter in 55.93.
"I was a lot slower than Amiez on the lower part of the course," said Sykora, who was forced to wait before pushing out of the start hut because of blustery conditions.
"But anything can happen on the second run.
Tomba, the first man out of the start hut, brought to life the thousands of fans lining the course and some even hanging from the floodlight pylons.
The crowd, the largest of the championships which close later on Saturday, cheered their hero's every move and waved signs, one of which read: 'Tomba you are immortal'.
But the flamboyant Italian's first leg time of 56.21 left the triple Olympic gold medallist in seventh place.
Amiez followed down the slope immediately afterwards and the crowd suddenly fell silent at the gulf between them.

Tomba's succesful arrival in the finish area marked the departure of much of the crowd who, having seen what they had come to see on a freezing evening, headed for bars and restaurants to warm up before the second run at 2000 GMT.
The slalom is the last race of the world championships and also Tomba's last chance of a medal in Italy.
Winner of the slalom and giant slalom titles last year, he failed to finish the giant on Wednesday.
